- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.3), model underreacts to upward momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the 20–30 day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 0.8–1.2% to forecast to compensate for lagged sentiment effect.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, don’t assume continuation — model often fails to recognize mean reversion in 10+ day horizons.
